profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility EWR11, at 3 Corporate Place, Piscataway Township, NJ 08854. Digital Realty's own property listing confirms this address as EWR11, but this session's fetch did not return a confirmed square footage figure for it specifically.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's New York/New Jersey metro footprint, which spans historic Manhattan carrier hotels and a cluster of suburban New Jersey buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township, coded EWR10 through EWR21 on the company's own metro listing. Digital Realty markets these properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and Silicon Valley, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. PSE&G serves most of the central New Jersey data center market.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than by individual building, and this pattern is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, not specific to this entry.

reading.body:
Digital Realty operates a multi-building data center campus in the New York/New Jersey region, with EWR11 located in Piscataway Township as one of at least three confirmed facilities in the metro area.

The facility's capacity in megawatts remains unconfirmed from tier-1 sources. Digital Realty's own site confirms the address and general location but does not publish per-building power consumption. This gap matters because power consumption is the direct constraint on AI workload placement. A data center's existence does not tell you whether it can support incremental AI compute demand or whether it is already saturated.

The Piscataway location sits within New Jersey's EWR metro cluster, part of the larger Northeast corridor infrastructure. Geographic clustering of multiple facilities under one operator can indicate shared power infrastructure or grid interconnection, though the data does not confirm whether EWR11, EWR12, and EWR21 draw from a common utility connection or independent feeds.

Researchers tracking AI infrastructure capacity should note that operator websites remain incomplete for power planning. Capacity data requires utility filings, real estate databases, or direct operator disclosure. The research status marked as "complete" reflects address confirmation only, not the power constraint that actually determines the facility's role in AI scaling.
